arxiv-2012-10733.title: Attraction and condensation of driven tracers in a narrow channel
arxiv-2012-10733.creator: Asaf Miron 1 , David Mukamel 1 and Harald A Posch 2
arxiv-2012-10733.description: Abstract Emergent bath-mediated attraction and condensation arise when multiple particles are simultaneously driven through an equilibrated bath under geometric constraints. While such scenarios are observed in a variety of non-equilibrium phenomena with an abundance of experimental and numerical evidence, little quantitative understanding of how these interactions arise is currently available.

arxiv-2012-14496.title: Guided accumulation of active particles by topological design of a second-order skin effect
arxiv-2012-14496.creator: Lucas S. Palacios, Serguei Tchoumakov, Maria Guix, Ignacio Pagonabarraga, Samuel Sánchez ∗, Adolfo G. Grushin ∗
arxiv-2012-14496.description: Abstract Abstract Collective guidance of out-of-equilibrium systems without using external fields is a challenge of paramount importance in active matter, ranging from bacterial colonies to swarms of self-propelled particles. Designing strategies to guide active matter and exploiting enhanced diffusion associated to its motion will provide insights for application from sensing, drug delivery to water remediation.

arxiv-2203-07074.title: The Born rule in a timeless Universe
arxiv-2203-07074.creator: Ovidiu Racorean
arxiv-2203-07074.description: Abstract In canonical quantization of gravity the wave function of the universe is CPT invariant. Thus, if the quantum state of the universe contains a particular history, than it must contain, with the same probability, the time-reversed image of that history as well.

arxiv-2406-11881.title: A non-autonomous framework for climate change and extreme weather events increase in a stochastic energy balance model
arxiv-2406-11881.creator: Gianmarco Del Sarto, Franco Flandoli
arxiv-2406-11881.description: Abstract We develop a three-timescale framework for modelling climate change and introduce a space-heterogeneous one-dimensional energy balance model. This model, addressing temperature fluctuations from rising carbon dioxide levels and the super-greenhouse effect in tropical regions, fits within the setting of stochastic reaction-diffusion equations.

arxiv-2409-15121.title: Rank-based stochastic differential inclusions and diffusion limits for a load balancing model
arxiv-2409-15121.creator: Rami Atar, Tomoyuki Ichiba
arxiv-2409-15121.description: Abstract . In [ 4 ] , a randomized load balancing model was studied in a heavy traffic asymptotic regime where the load balancing stream is thin compared to the total arrival stream. It was shown that the limit is given by a system of rank-based Brownian particles on the half-line.

arxiv-2409-18247.title: A Broadband X-ray Investigation of Fast-Spinning Intermediate Polar CTCV J2056–3014
arxiv-2409-18247.creator: Ciro Salcedo, Kaya Mori, Gabriel Bridges, Charles J. Hailey, David A. H. Buckley, Raimundo Lopes de Oliveira, Gavin Ramsay, Anke van Dyk
arxiv-2409-18247.description: Abstract We report on XMM-Newton , NuSTAR , and NICER X-ray observations of CTCV J2056-3014, a cataclysmic variable (CV) with one of the fastest-spinning white dwarfs (WDs) at P = 29.6 P=29.6 s. While previously classified as an intermediate polar (IP), CJ2056 also exhibits the properties of WZ-Sge-type CVs, such as dwarf novae and superoutbursts.

arxiv-2410-01979.title: Auto-conditioned primal-dual hybrid gradient method and alternating direction method of multipliers Thanks: This research was partially supported by Air Force Office of Scientific Research grant FA9550-22-1-0447. Coauthors of this paper are listed according to the alphabetic order.
arxiv-2410-01979.creator: Guanghui Lan, Tianjiao Li
arxiv-2410-01979.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Guanghui Lan, Tianjiao Li. Line search procedures are often employed in primal-dual methods for bilinear saddle point problems, especially when the norm of the linear operator is large or difficult to compute. In this paper, we demonstrate that line search is unnecessary by introducing a novel primal-dual method, the auto-conditioned primal-dual hybrid gradient (AC-PDHG) method, which achieves optimal complexity for solving bilinear saddle point problems. AC-PDHG is fully adaptive to the linear operator, using only past iterates to estimate its norm.

arxiv-2501-17023.title: Asymmetric dual cascade in gravitational wave turbulence Journal: Physica D
arxiv-2501-17023.creator: Benoît Gay, Sébastien Galtier
arxiv-2501-17023.description: Abstract We numerically simulate, in both the forced and decay regimes, a fourth-order nonlinear diffusion equation derived from the kinetic equation of gravitational wave turbulence in the limit of strongly local quartic interactions. When a forcing is applied to an intermediate wavenumber k i k_{i} , we observe a dual cascade of energy and wave action.

arxiv-2507-15386.title: Learning to Gridize: Segment Physical World by Wireless Communication Channel
arxiv-2507-15386.creator: Juntao Wang, Feng Yin, Tian Ding, Tsung-Hui Chang, Zhi-Quan Luo, and Qi Yan
arxiv-2507-15386.description: Abstract Gridization, the process of partitioning space into grids where users share similar channel characteristics, serves as a fundamental prerequisite for efficient large-scale network optimization. However, existing methods like Geographical or Beam Space Gridization (GSG or BSG) are limited by reliance on unavailable location data or the flawed assumption that similar signal strengths imply similar channel properties.

arxiv-2507-22595.title: On string theory on deformed BTZ and T ​ T ¯ + J ​ T ¯ + T ​ J ¯ T\bar{T}+J\bar{T}+T\bar{J}
arxiv-2507-22595.description: Abstract Aspects of superstring theory on black-strings backgrounds, corresponding to deformed BTZ black holes, formed near k k N ​ S ​ 5 NS5 branes by p p fundamental strings, and single-trace T ​ T ¯ + J ​ T ¯ + T ​ J ¯ T\bar{T}+J\bar{T}+T\bar{J} holography, are presented.

arxiv-2509-17975.title: Optimal local basis truncation of lattice quantum many-body systems
arxiv-2509-17975.creator: Peter Majcen, Giovanni Cataldi, Pietro Silvi, Simone Montangero
arxiv-2509-17975.description: Abstract We show how to optimally reduce the local Hilbert basis of lattice quantum many-body (QMB) Hamiltonians. The basis truncation exploits the most relevant eigenvalues of the estimated single-site reduced density matrix (RDM). It is accurate and numerically stable across different model phases, even close to quantum phase transitions.

It is primarily composed of cellulose, hemicellulose, and lignin, which are strongly associated with each other. Pretreatment processes are mainly involved in effective...

pmc-10803615.title: Investigating autism knowledge, self-efficacy, and confidence following maternal and child health nurse training for the early identification of autism
pmc-10803615.creator: Katherine Gore, Melissa Gilbert, Marguerite Hawke, Josephine Barbaro
pmc-10803615.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). IntroductionEarly identification of children with a high likelihood of autism can lead to referral for diagnostic services and access to early supports, resulting in improved outcomes for children and families. Maternal and Child Health Nurses (MCHNs) in Victoria, Australia, are well-placed to monitor infants and toddlers for signs of autism, given children and caregivers attend free, regular, well-baby consultations from birth through to school age.

pmc-11494966.title: Is the identification of caseating granuloma in the intestine indicative of tuberculosis? a rare case of Crohn’s disease
pmc-11494966.creator: Siqi Tao, Yan Chen, Wen Hu, Keren Shen, Jinghong Xu
pmc-11494966.description: BackgroundCrohn’s disease (CD) is a chronic intestinal inflammatory disorder, the etiology of which remains unknown, and is characterized by symptoms such as chronic abdominal pain, diarrhea, obstruction, and perianal lesions. Histopathology is widely regarded as the preferred method for diagnosing CD, although the histological diagnosis may lack specificity.

pmc-11790453.title: Fibroblasts in rheumatoid arthritis: novel roles in joint inflammation and beyond
pmc-11790453.creator: Elpida Neofotistou-Themeli, Panagiota Goutakoli, Theodoros Chanis, Maria Semitekolou, Eirini Sevdali, Prodromos Sidiropoulos
pmc-11790453.description: High-throughput technologies in human and animal studies have revealed novel molecular and cellular pathways involved in tissue inflammation of rheumatoid arthritis (RA). Fibroblasts have been in the forefront of research for several decades. Subpopulations with specific phenotypic and functional properties have been characterized both in mouse models and human disease.

pmc-12469406.title: Clinical Characteristics and Risk Factors for Severe Exacerbation in Never-Smokers with Chronic Obstructive Pulmonary Disease: A Retrospective Cohort Study
pmc-12469406.creator: Josep Montserrat-Capdevila, Pilar Vaqué Castilla, Yoseba Cánovas Zaldúa, Francesc Alòs, Joan Deniel-Rosanas, Pere Simonet, Pau Olivares-Sanzo, Jennyfer Jiménez Díaz, Sandra Moreno Garcia, Araceli Fuentes, Eugeni Paredes, Pere Godoy
pmc-12469406.description: Background: Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) in nonsmokers is increasingly recognized, yet its clinical profile and outcomes remain less well defined compared to smoking-related COPD. The aim of this study was to compare the clinical characteristics, comorbidities, and risk factors associated with severe exacerbations in nonsmoking COPD patients versus smokers.

pmc-12472367.title: Association Between Multi-Dimensional Sleep Health and Breakfast Skipping in Japanese High School Students
pmc-12472367.creator: Suzune Nagao, Yuh Sasawaki, Hitoshi Inokawa, Nobuko Kitagawa, Naoyuki Takashima, Kazuhiro Yagita, Emanuela Gualdi-Russo, Luciana Zaccagni
pmc-12472367.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). Background/Objectives: Breakfast skipping has been associated with a wide range of adverse health outcomes, including metabolic disorders, disrupted circadian rhythm, and impairments of memory and attention in adolescents and adults. Although partial associations between sleep and breakfast behaviors have been reported, few studies have examined multi-dimensional sleep health simultaneously in relation to breakfast skipping, especially comprehensive studies systematically examining this relationship, particularly under controlled social conditions, remain insufficient.

pmc-12771143.title: A risk prediction model for autism spectrum disorder integrating biopsychosocial factors: a systematic review and meta-analysis with multicenter validation
pmc-12771143.creator: Lu Zhang, Weicong He, Pujue Huang, Lisha Zhong
pmc-12771143.description: BackgroundEarly identification of individuals at high risk for autism spectrum disorder (ASD) is crucial for optimizing intervention strategies and improving outcomes. This study aims to develop a risk prediction model integrating biopsychosocial factors through a systematic review with multicenter validation.MethodsA comprehensive search was conducted across PubMed, Cochrane Library, and Embase for articles on biopsychosocial ASD risk factors during 2010–2023.

pmc-12805769.title: Urbanization and landscape effects on taxonomic and functional wild bee diversity in small towns and rural areas
pmc-12805769.creator: Weronika Banaszak-Cibicka, Łukasz Dylewski, Joanna Bajon, Joanna T Białas, Monika Fliszkiewicz
pmc-12805769.description: BackgroundPlanning and managing urban landscapes for greater biodiversity and creating effective conservation strategies requires understanding the relationships between biodiversity and different types of urbanization. Here, we described the variation between small-town and rural areas in two dimensions of biodiversity – taxonomic and functional.

pmc-13077457.title: Pulmonary toxicity of immune checkpoint inhibitors
pmc-13077457.creator: Sean Garvey, Parthiban Nadarajan
pmc-13077457.description: Immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs) have brought about major advances in the treatment of cancer over the past 15 years. With a growing armoury of these immunotherapies available and an ever-expanding list of indications for their use, ICIs have become a standard of care in the treatment of cancers including nonsmall cell lung cancer, melanoma and renal cell carcinoma.

pmc-13273929.title: Tuning the Affinity of Chimeric Antigen Receptors Enhances the Function of Human Engineered Regulatory T Cells
pmc-13273929.creator: Ada Sera Kurt, Marwa Elgosbi, Elisavet Kodela, Emmanuelle Landmann, Paula Ruiz, Yoh Zen, Jorge Torres‐Yaguana, Alexander Puttick, Quisha Bustamante, Minahil Sharjeel, Hannan Murshid, Marc Martinez‐Llordella, Alberto Sanchez‐Fueyo
pmc-13273929.description: Chimeric antigen receptors (CAR) incorporating single‐chain variable fragments (scFv) exhibit much higher affinity for their cognate antigens than native T cell receptors (TCR). Reducing the affinity of the CAR has been shown to improve the function of effector CAR‐T cells by limiting their activation‐induced exhaustion while preserving their capacity for serial killing of antigen‐rich tumor cells.

pmc-13311984.title: Esketamine improves postoperative sleep quality in thoracic surgery patients with preoperative sleep disturbance: a randomized controlled trial
pmc-13311984.creator: Xingyu Wang, Haijin Wang, Huiyu Luo

pmc-13549969.title: Hereditary cancer: Germline testing practices across ERN GENTURIS member countries
pmc-13549969.creator: Milena Kiljańczyk, Zanda Daneberga, Mikk Tooming, Katarzyna Urbańczyk, Minna Pöyhönen, Tiina Kahre, Lenka Foretova, Emma Tham, Tamara Milagre, Béla Melegh, Maria K Haanpää, Ana Blatnik, Katharina Wimmer, Robin de Putter, Karin Wadt, Claude Houdayer, Elke Holinski-Feder, Antonis Kattamis, Barbara Kli
pmc-13549969.description: Germline genetic testing practices for hereditary cancer vary across the European Reference Network on Genetic Tumour Risk Syndromes (ERN GENTURIS) member countries. We surveyed experts in genetic testing from 20 EU member countries and Norway to assess multi-gene panel usage, availability of genome-wide sequencing, first-tier testing approaches, implementation of polygenic risk scores, and the roles of non-genetic healthcare professionals.

uslaw-usc-t26-s6303.title: 26 U.S.C. § 6303 — Notice and demand for tax
uslaw-usc-t26-s6303.creator: United States Congress
uslaw-usc-t26-s6303.description: United States Code, Title 26 (Internal Revenue Code); Chapter 64 (Collection); Subchapter A (General Provisions). Current through Public Law 119-134, as published by the Office of the Law Revision Counsel. (a) General rule Where it is not otherwise provided by this title, the Secretary shall, as soon as practicable, and within 60 days, after the making of an assessment of a tax pursuant to section 6203, give notice to each person liable.

uslaw-usc-t40-s15307.title: 40 U.S.C. § 15307 — Tribal participation
uslaw-usc-t40-s15307.creator: United States Congress
uslaw-usc-t40-s15307.description: United States Code, Title 40 (Public Buildings, Property, And Works); Chapter 153 (Regional Commissions). Current through Public Law 119-134, as published by the Office of the Law Revision Counsel. Governments of Indian tribes in the region of the Southwest Border Regional Commission shall be allowed to participate in matters before that Commission in the same manner and to the same extent as State agencies and instrumentalities in the region.
